communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Massachusetts Public Records Law, I hereby request the following records:

Dear Records Custodian:

This is a public records request pursuant to Mass. Gen. Laws ch. 66, § 10A. I hereby request the following records.

I hereby request an excel/CSV extraction containing records of all shifts worked by all Boston Police Department employees from 1/1/2025 to 12/31/2025. Please include the following fields of information:

City of Boston Employee ID (6 digit ID)
Employee first name
Employee last name
Employee middle name or initial
Assigned description 
Charged description
Start time
End time
Worked hours
Billed hours


I understand that you are not required to create a new public record to comply with my request, see, e.g., ch. 66, §6A(d), however, extraction of data from a database or electronic record system does not constitute creating a new record. See Att’y Gen. v. Dist. Att’y for Plymouth Dist., 484 Mass. 260, 275 (2020) (“[W]here public records are in electronic form, . . . a public records request that requires a government entity to search its electronic database to extract requested data does not mean that the extracted data constitute the creation of a new record under the public records law.”); see also 950 Mass. Code Regs. 32.07(1)(f).

Please produce the records in an electronically-accessible format, including for screen readers, excel, or CSV. See 950 Mass. Code. Regs. 32.04(5)(d). Files that are not accessible to screen readers include, for example, .pdf files or physical documents.

I request fees be waived as my request is in the public interest. See ch. 66, § 10(d)(v); 950 Mass. Code Regs. 32.07(k). “All agencies and municipalities are strongly urged to waive fees associated with access to public records.” This request will contribute to the public’s understanding of the Boston Police Department and is not in my commercial interest. Namely, these records will be made available to the public on Muckrock.com and will be used to update the Boston Police Index, a long-term community collaboration aimed to enhance transparency and accountability of the Boston Police Department through meticulous data collection and analysis. Thus, disclosure of these records will significantly contribute to the public’s understanding of the Boston Police Department’s operations.

If you do not waive the fees associated with my request, please provide a written, itemized, good faith estimate and explanation of the fees prior to fulfilling my request. See 950 Mass. Code Regs. 32.0792)(b); see also ch. 66, § 10(e) (“A records access officer shall not charge a fee for a public record unless the records access officer responded to the requestor within 10 business days.”).

If you believe any of the records I have requested are exempt from disclosure, please identify both: (1) the records, categories of records, or portions of the records you intend to withhold; and (2) the specific reasons for such withholding, including the specific exemption you are relying on. See ch. 66, § 10(b)(iv).

If necessary to comply with my request, I welcome your suggested modifications pursuant to ch. 66, § 10(b)(vii) and 950 Mass. Code Regs. 32.06(2)(g). I am available to discuss any proposed modifications at adasuss@bu.edu.

I also request that, if appropriate, fees be waived as we believe this request is in the public interest, as suggested but not stipulated by the recommendations of the Massachusetts Supervisor of Public Records. The requested documents will be made available to the general public free of charge as part of the public information service at MuckRock.com, and is not made for commercial usage.

I expect the request to be filled in an accessible format, including for screen readers, which provide text-to-speech for persons unable to read print. Files that are not accessible to screen readers include, for example, .pdf image files as well as physical documents.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 10 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

ada sussman

communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Illinois Freedom of Information Act., I hereby request the following records:

For William Claude Reavis Math and Science Specialty School (834 E. 50th St, Chicago, IL) for the period of March 1, 2022 through August 31, 2022,  I am requesting:

1. Incident and Disciplinary Records: Copies of all Incident Reports, Student Code of Conduct (SCC) Referrals, Disciplinary Notices, and Misconduct Reports generated at the school level during the requested timeframe. (Please note: Do not deny this request on the basis that a specific "Safety and Security Department" database does not exist. As your office previously stated in unrelated requests,  these records are generated and stored at the school level. I am requesting those specific school-level documents).

2. Audit Trails and Metadata: Any existing audit trails, system metadata, modification histories, or access logs for the records described in Item #1. This includes the date and time the record was created or modified.

3. Staff Identifiers: The full name, official job title/position, CPS-issued email address, and CPS system User ID of the CPS employee(s) who created, edited, modified, or accessed the records described in Item #1. 

PREEMPTIVE CLARIFICATIONS AND WAIVERS (PLEASE READ CAREFULLY):
• NO STUDENT PRIVACY ISSUES: I am NOT requesting any student names, student ID numbers, initials, or any other Personally Identifiable Information (PII) regarding any student. You are fully authorized and expected to redact all student information. I am strictly requesting the underlying narrative of the events (with student names redacted as "Student A", etc.), the rule violated, the disciplinary action taken, and the adult staff members involved.

• NO PERSONAL EMPLOYEE PRIVACY ISSUES: I am waiving any request for personal employee information, including home addresses, personal cell phone numbers, Social Security numbers, dates of birth, or personal (non-CPS) email addresses.
• OFFICIAL CAPACITY: I am only requesting the CPS-issued professional email address, CPS system User ID, and official job title of the staff members. Under Illinois FOIA precedent, public employees acting in their official capacity (using government systems and credentials) do not have a protectable privacy interest in their official actions. Therefore, Exemption 7(1)(b) does not apply to the release of a public employee's name, official title, government email, or User ID. 

PROCEDURAL SAFEGUARDS:
• No "Unduly Burdensome" Denial: If you believe this request is unduly burdensome, Illinois law (5 ILCS 140/3(g)) requires you to communicate with me to narrow the request before denying it. I am willing to discuss narrowing the scope to specific incident types if necessary.
• Redaction over Withholding: If any portion of a responsive record is deemed exempt, you are required to redact only that specific portion and release the remainder of the document. You may not withhold an entire document because a name is present.
• Data Dictionary: If you claim that the systems used to store these records (e.g., ASPEN, ICT) do not possess an audit trail or modification history, please provide the "Data Dictionary" or System Administrator Manual for the software that proves the system does not track this information.
• Fallback for Staff Names: If you determine that the actual name of an employee must be redacted, you are still required to provide their official job title/position, their CPS email address, their User ID, and the date/time of their action. The public has a right to know the role of the official altering public records. 

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes. I request that the records be provided electronically via email attachment in Excel or PDF format. If there are any fees, please inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request.

Thank you for your interest in Chicago Public Schools. Your FOIA request has been submitted. Your FOIA Center reference number for tracking purposes is: N020816-111026 
You have requested the following records: To Whom It May Concern: 

Pursuant to the Illinois Freedom of Information Act., I hereby request the following records: 

For William Claude Reavis Math and Science Specialty School (834 E. 50th St, Chicago, IL) for the period of March 1, 2022 through August 31, 2022, I am requesting: 

1. Incident and Disciplinary Records: Copies of all Incident Reports, Student Code of Conduct (SCC) Referrals, Disciplinary Notices, and Misconduct Reports generated at the school level during the requested timeframe. (Please note: Do not deny this request on the basis that a specific "Safety and Security Department" database does not exist. As your office previously stated in unrelated requests, these records are generated and stored at the school level. I am requesting those specific school-level documents). 

2. Audit Trails and Metadata: Any existing audit trails, system metadata, modification histories, or access logs for the records described in Item #1. This includes the date and time the record was created or modified. 

3. Staff Identifiers: The full name, official job title/position, CPS-issued email address, and CPS system User ID of the CPS employee(s) who created, edited, modified, or accessed the records described in Item #1. 

PREEMPTIVE CLARIFICATIONS AND WAIVERS (PLEASE READ CAREFULLY): 
• NO STUDENT PRIVACY ISSUES: I am NOT requesting any student names, student ID numbers, initials, or any other Personally Identifiable Information (PII) regarding any student. You are fully authorized and expected to redact all student information. I am strictly requesting the underlying narrative of the events (with student names redacted as "Student A", etc.), the rule violated, the disciplinary action taken, and the adult staff members involved. 

• NO PERSONAL EMPLOYEE PRIVACY ISSUES: I am waiving any request for personal employee information, including home addresses, personal cell phone numbers, Social Security numbers, dates of birth, or personal (non-CPS) email addresses. 
• OFFICIAL CAPACITY: I am only requesting the CPS-issued professional email address, CPS system User ID, and official job title of the staff members. Under Illinois FOIA precedent, public employees acting in their official capacity (using government systems and credentials) do not have a protectable privacy interest in their official actions. Therefore, Exemption 7(1)(b) does not apply to the release of a public employee's name, official title, government email, or User ID.

• Redaction over Withholding: If any portion of a responsive record is deemed exempt, you are required to redact only that specific portion and release the remainder of the document. You may not withhold an entire document because a name is present. 
• Data Dictionary: If you claim that the systems used to store these records (e.g., ASPEN, ICT) do not possess an audit trail or modification history, please provide the "Data Dictionary" or System Administrator Manual for the software that proves the system does not track this information. 
• Fallback for Staff Names: If you determine that the actual name of an employee must be redacted, you are still required to provide their official job title/position, their CPS email address, their User ID, and the date/time of their action. The public has a right to know the role of the official altering public records.

title: Traffic Analytics for America.gov

communications.subject: Freedom of Information Act Request: Traffic Analytics for America.gov
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Freedom of Information Act, I hereby request the following records:

Unlike many other websites operated by the federal government, America.gov does not participate in the Digital Analytics Program (DAP), which is also administered by the GSA. This means that it does not contribute any data on its website traffic to https://analytics.usa.gov/, which undermines trust in claims about its popularity or effectiveness for the American public.

I would like to request the following documentation for FOIA purposes:
1. Any communications related to why America.gov does not include any analytics capability provided by DAP.
2. Any internal measurements of America.gov traffic that have been tracked by GSA. These might include both web analytics or it might also include data about chats initiated every week to the Large Language Models (LLMs) that power AI chats on the site (I believe it might be xAI Grok and/or Google Gemini)

I would expect this information would be provided as briefing materials to senior staff via email and could be found by searching for words like "traffic" or "analytics", etc. and "America.gov" I would expect these emails and communications to be from early-mid 2026 or later.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 20 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Jacob Harris

Thank you so much for your time and help. We really appreciate it.

Warmly,
Logan

communications.subject: Nevada Public Records Act Request: Axon Draft One Records
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Nevada Public Records Act, I hereby request the following records related to the use of any AI-assisted police report technology provided by the company Axon (previously known as Taser). This technology may be referred to as Draft One (https://www.axon.com/products/draft-one), the Axon Narrative Assistant, Axon AI, or by another name. 

For more information on the Axon Narrative Assistant, please refer to the User Guide found at this link: https://www.documentcloud.org/documents/25418151-axon-narrative-assistant-user-guide_axon-records-1-1/. 

For more information on Axon Draft One, please look at this page on the Axon website: https://www.axon.com/resources/closer-look-draft-one. 

CONTRACT AND AGREEMENTS

1.  All contracts, memorandums of understanding, and any other written agreements between this agency and Axon related to the use of Axon AI, Axon Draft One, Narrative Assistant, or any other AI-assisted report generation tool provided by Axon. 

Responsive records include all associated amendments, exhibits, and supplemental and supporting documentation. 

If access to Draft One, Axon AI or similar tools is being provided via an existing contract or through an informal agreement, please provide the relevant contract or the relevant communication or agreement that facilitated the access. This includes all agreements, both formal and informal, including all trial access, even if that access does not or did not involve financial obligations. 

2. All relevant terms of use, licensing agreements, and any other guiding materials;

TRAINING, POLICIES and USE MATERIAL

3. All training materials relevant to Draft One, Axon AI or Axon Narrative Assistant generated by this agency; 

4. All training material provided by Axon to this agency regarding its use of Draft One; 

5. All user manuals, other guidance materials, help documents, or related materials;

6. Guides, safety tests, and other supplementary material that mention Draft One provided by Axon from January 1, 2024 and the date this request is received;

7. All final reports, evaluations, reports, or other documentation concluding or summarizing a trial or evaluation period or pilot project; 

8. Any and all policies related to the use of Draft One, the Narrative Assistant, or any other AI-assisted report generation offerings provided by Axon (An example of one such policy can be found here: https://cdn.muckrock.com/foia_files/2024/11/26/608_Computer_Software_and_Transcription-Assisted_Report_Generation.pdf);


COMMUNICATIONS
9. All communications sent or received by any representative of this agency with individuals representing Axon referencing the following term, including emails and attachments: 
• Draft One
• Narrative Assistant
• AI-generated report
• Axon AI

10. All communications sent to or received by any representative of this agency with each of the following email addresses, including attachments:
a. draftone@axon.com
b. bryan@axon.com
c. noahsw@axon.com               	 
d. efleischli@axon.com (Erin Fleischli)
e. edriver@axon.com

g. gsigman@axon.com (Gabriel Sigman, Technical Account Manager)
h. tstuhr@axon.com (Tierney Stuhr, Sales Representative)

a. garlocks@reno.gov (Sean Garlock, Assistant Chief of Police)

We ask that these materials be provided on a rolling basis; as your office collects and reviews records, we would appreciate it if your office would provide those materials to us incrementally. If possible, please provide any responsive contractual and financial materials within the statutorily-mandated public record law time frame. We would prefer communications to be provided next. Please contact us for further discussion regarding the search and release of these materials.

This request is not being made for commercial purposes. Please assess fees appropriately in accordance with a public records request being made in the public interest.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform us of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I request that all records be disclosed in their native, digital format and transmitted to us electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or by CD-ROM if not.

If you need any more information in order to process the request, or cannot process a portion of the request for any reason, please respond to the email address on this request or “cabrerjess@gmail.com”. Further discussion may be conducted via email. Please let us know if a phone call will be necessary or desirable; such contact information will be provided upon request.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 5 business days, as the statute requires business days.

Sincerely, 
Jesse Cabrera
